title: Capsular Contracture: Symptoms, Grades and Treatment
meta_description: Scar tissue tightens around an implant. Baker grades I to IV, 10-year rates from 12.1% to 20.8% by maker, normal firmness vs when to call, and treatment.
excerpt: Capsular contracture is scar tissue tightening around a breast implant. Here are the four Baker grades, how to tell normal firmness from a reason to call, 10-year rates with their exact sources, what the evidence says about massage and surgery, and what is still unknown.
quick_answer:
What is capsular contracture?

Capsular contracture is when scar tissue around a breast implant tightens and hardens. The FDA grades it I to IV; III and IV are considered severe and may need surgery. Within 10 years of a first augmentation, severe contracture was 12.1% in Mentor's study and 13% in Sientra's. The FDA says the cause is not known.

images.text_in_image:
The Baker Grades of Capsular Contracture

Grade I: Breast is normally soft and looks natural
Grade II: Breast is a little firm but looks normal
Grade III: Breast is firm and looks abnormal
Grade IV: Breast is hard, painful, and looks abnormal

Grades III and IV are considered severe and may require reoperation.

Source: FDA

Usually normal while you heal

sources.title: Risks and Complications of Breast Implants
quotes: Capsular contracture is the hardening of the breast around the implant. It can occur in the tissue surrounding one or both implants. This hardening causes the tissue to tighten, which can be painful.
Capsular contracture may be more common following infection, hematoma and seroma. However, the cause of capsular contracture is not known.
Grade I: Breast is normally soft and looks natural
Grade II: Breast is a little firm but looks normal
Grade III: Breast is firm and looks abnormal
Grade IV: Breast is hard, painful, and looks abnormal
Grades III and IV capsular contracture are considered severe and may require reoperation.
Capsular contracture could occur again after surgery to correct it.
The FDA has not cleared or approved any devices to treat or reduce the incidence of capsular contracture.

Collection of fluid around the implant. May cause swelling, pain and bruising.

No price stated: the cost line links the procedure page #pricing. Miami queries (capsular contracture miami, 181 impressions at 47.8; treatment miami, 105 at 55.6) are left out on purpose: no Miami in the title, and the practice's revision policy is unconfirmed. Uses 'one in six' only to explain it, per the bank's writer note; 51.7% stays out as an illustrative maximum; Tehrani's lifetime-risk figures and '75% within two years' stay out; Aspen ultrasound stays out; 'massage for life' appears only as a claim the evidence doesn't support. Natrelle saline 20.8% is PASS survey data and is labeled that way. consistency.py '?' lines are figures with their own sources in sources[] (5.9, 9.7, 12.9 Sientra; 20.8 Allergan; 10.6 Headon; 25 Headon; 31 and 40 Sood). Links to other new posts (/blog/breast-implants-over-or-under-the-muscle, /blog/saline-vs-silicone-breast-implants, /blog/how-long-do-breast-implants-last) mean those go live in the same run or before. cta stays default because the 'breast' CTA copy says 'our board-certified surgeons'. Fact check batch 4 applied 2026-11-03: sudden-swelling attribution split between MedlinePlus and the FDA, unsourced call-your-surgeon lines labeled practical advice, irrigation evidence shown as mixed (Clark, Headon, Calobrace), onset line now 'we did not find a reliable figure', Li's figure stated against the breast fold and not the armpit. Calobrace 2018 also lists the surgical bra as a risk factor; left out on purpose as an unexplained association that could lead readers to stop wearing one against every recovery source.
